current_traces.claim: Native skill names/bars are projected from existing records; visibility remains gated by native unlock and visibility threshold; presentation helper avoids XP-creating getters.

Current methods-and-practice panel enumerates registered discovery/learn/practice/use/recovery commands, previews each action, filters on visibility, marks known terms/reasons, retains only player-side observations and reports accepted work using authoritative clock difference.

Simulation commands are authored and registry-bound, preview checks actor/role/world/location/target/co-location/busy/life/once/claim/site conditions, then validates costs, effects and weighted outcomes on candidate copies. Commit re-previews synchronously, spends means and freezes outcome/command identity for accepted jobs.

Inventory effects use native inventory binding or simulation-owned stock; consumed borrowed items are rejected unless an explicit custody break policy is supplied; equipment cannot be consumed while equipped. Custody is validated as an owned record keyed to owner/holder/item/count/time.

Expansion persistence validates a full future envelope, stages native skill/item/unlock/equipment reconstruction, writes the existing envelope durably, and only then updates live expansion/native owners and UI projections.

Save envelope validates version, expansion and realm domains, retired content, owner inventory/XP consistency and optional NPC equipment before real-loader preflight; import writes only after preflight succeeds. This is static code evidence, not a newly executed save/reload result.

Current Makeable-now recipe visibility is a read-only projection over existing unlocked rows, station tier, known exact materials and consumable stock; it preserves selected/focused rows during final-input consumption and does not create craft results or grant rewards.
Native action button name currently uses action_name (the earlier FNA01 report's starting_text mismatch is stale); unrelated activity/dialogue surfaces still legitimately use starting_text.
